title: Rapid roleplay scripts & metrics backstop (seller ops workshop)
content:
Context:
Quick workshop notes and working scripts for SE/CS roleplays focused on out-of-the-gate pilot demos and rapid fallback troubleshooting. Purpose is to: 1) give sellers short, repeatable roleplay scripts they can run in 10–12 minutes, 2) define minimal metrics to collect during pilots so Ops/Eng can triage regressions quickly, and 3) provide a lightweight rubric for scoring pilot success.

How to use this doc (TL;DR):
- Run 2 roleplays per week per AE/SE pair during pilot week.
- Capture the three pilot metrics after each session in the shared pilot spreadsheet (linked).
- If metric X deviates, run fallback recipe A (script below) and log incident.

Session outline (10–12 min):
- 00:00–00:60s intro + context (customer persona + pain).
- 01:00–04:00 discovery + qualification script (see Discovery Script).
- 04:00–08:00 live demo + intentional failure (trigger a degraded model/latency scenario).
- 08:00–10:00 fallback + remediation script.
- 10:00–12:00 debrief + metric capture.

Discovery script (short form):
- Opener: "Quick context — we help teams serve high-quality LLM responses with predictable cost/latency. What's a recent customer experience where latency or hallucination caused friction for you?"
- Clarify: "How many requests per minute at peak? What SLOs are non-negotiable (p95, p99)?"
- Constraint probe: "Are there regulatory or network constraints (VPC, on-prem, no external model calls)?"
- Outcome probe: "If this were solved, what would happen to your product metrics (retention, CTAs) in 90 days?"

Demo script (happy path -> intentional degradation):
- Start with hosted path: show simple generate/chat with Redwood API. Use model variant 'redwood-compact-v2' for throughput example.
- Show latency totals in Console (token-level breakdown). Say: "Notice how the batch cache cut per-token time by ~20%".
- Intentionally switch routing policy to dedicated pool (simulate capacity constraint): trigger "fallback to smaller quantized variant" and show degraded output (shorter, some truncation).
- Ask customer: "If you saw output like that under load, what would you tolerate?"

Fallback & remediation script (short step-by-step):
- If hallucination spikes: 1) Reduce temperature; 2) Route to a higher-quality model (e.g., 'redwood-qa-l1'); 3) Enable prefix-KV recall for the session.
- If latency p95 > SLA + 200ms: 1) Increase allowed batch window to 50ms (tradeoff note), 2) Route to regionally closer pool, or 3) Switch to cached response when prefix detected.
- If cost per token > target: 1) Enable inexpensive quantized fallback for low-priority routes, 2) Adjust max tokens and stop sequences.

Pilot metrics (minimal, capture after each session):
- Metric A: Demo-response latency p95 (ms) — record numeric.
- Metric B: Subjective quality score (1–5) from roleplay customer.
- Metric C: E2E recovery time (time to route + verified good output) when fallback invoked (seconds).
- Metric D: Cost delta observed during the session (tokens billed estimate).

Scoring rubric (quick):
- Green: p95 < SLA + 100ms, quality >=4, recovery time <30s.
- Yellow: p95 within SLA +200ms OR quality 3, recovery <90s.
- Red: p95 > SLA +200ms OR quality <=2 OR recovery >90s.

Roleplay scripts (short prompts for buyer personas):
1) Platform architect (concern: predictable throughput):
   - Prompt: "We need deterministic p99 under 250ms for inference. Walk me through how you'd configure Redwood to meet that."
   - Enabler replies: show dedicated pool config, autoscale policy, cache strategy.
2) Product manager (concern: hallucination/high precision):
   - Prompt: "We cannot tolerate hallucinated outputs in customer-facing summaries. What's your mitigation plan?"
   - Enabler replies: show temperature control, evals/scorecards, rollbacks, canary to smaller user cohort.
3) Security/compliance lead (concern: data residency):
   - Prompt: "All data must remain in our VPC, keys via customer KMS. How do you ensure we don't leak?"
   - Enabler replies: outline Private deployment, customer-managed CP, audit logs, HSM/KMS integration.

Common objections and short counters (for SEs):
- "We already have an LLM vendor": "What's your current pain — inconsistent p95 or unpredictable cost? We specialize in making inference predictable and economical with the same API across hosted/dedicated/private."
- "It’s too risky to switch models": "We support canary rollouts, A/B by route, and automated rollback on quality regressions — customers typically pilot in 2–4 weeks with measurable KPIs."
- "Quantized models lose accuracy": "Quantization profiles are suggested per workload; we recommend hybrid routing so critical routes stay high-precision while batch jobs use quantized variants."

Data capture template (copy into the pilot spreadsheet after each run):
- session_id, seller, date, persona, metricA_latency_ms, metricB_quality_1to5, metricC_recovery_s, metricD_cost_est_usd, notes

Ops escalation checklist (if Red):
- Tag ticket GTM-PILOT-RED, include session_id and logs.
- Pager SRE if recovery time > 5 minutes and p99 latency off by > 500ms.
- Run fallback flow and attach console trace + model variant used.

Open questions / TODOs from workshop:
- Add quick visual cheat for latency vs cost tradeoff (one-pager).
- Create a 60s explainer video for "what happens during fallback".
- Build a tiny dashboard view in Console that shows the four pilot metrics per session.

Links & references:
- Confluence: Pilot design doc (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: GTM pilot epic (JIRA-GTM-987)
- Repo: roleplay scripts and automation (github.com/redwood-inference/se-scripts)

Notes to self (fragmented):
- We should test the demo with a quantized variant that preserves hallucination rate — need eng input.
- Ask product about whether to expose a one-click "force fallback" in console for demos.
- Consider making the scoring rubric align with procurement acceptance criteria (CFO asks).

End of sketch — keep this light and iterate. Use this as the base for next week’s seller ops session.
